question: Uniqueness check and soft-delete interactions for ResourceType
claim: 1) ExistsByGroupAndNameAsync in both CreateResourceType and UpdateResourceType data providers calls `.IgnoreQueryFilters()` (bypassing the global DeletedAt==null query filter) but re-applies an explicit `t.DeletedAt == null` predicate in the same LINQ expression, so the net effect is that soft-deleted rows are excluded from the uniqueness check just as the global filter would exclude them — but the check itself never sees deleted-row data implicitly, it's explicit. 2) The unique index on resource_types(GroupId, Name), defined both in ResourceTypeConfiguration.cs and in migration 20260514155140_AddResourceTypeUniqueAndCursorIndexes.cs and reflected in the model snapshot, is NOT filtered (no HasFilter/filter argument) — it is a plain `.IsUnique()` index covering all rows regardless of DeletedAt. This differs from resource_instances(GroupId, Id) and management_groups(OwnerId, Name), which both use `HasFilter("\"DeletedAt\" IS NULL")` partial unique/lookup indexes. 3) IgnoreQueryFilters() call sites on ResourceTypes in Resources.Core (non-test) code: CreateResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.ExistsByGroupAndNameAsync (duplicate-name check, explicitly re-filters DeletedAt==null), UpdateResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.ExistsByGroupAndNameAsync (same pattern), and DeleteResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.SoftDeleteInstancesAsync which calls IgnoreQueryFilters on ResourceInstances (not ResourceTypes) to reach already non-deleted instances for cascading soft-delete, filtering `DeletedAt == null` explicitly. No other ResourceTypes.IgnoreQueryFilters() call sites exist in Resources.Core; GroupDeletedHandler.cs uses IgnoreQueryFilters on GroupReadModels/GroupMemberReadModels, not ResourceTypes. GetResourceInstancesQueryDataProvider uses IgnoreQueryFilters conditionally on ResourceInstances for an includeDeleted query option, unrelated to ResourceType. 4) CreateResourceInstanceCommandHandler resolves the resource type via `_dataProvider.GetResourceTypeAsync(command.ResourceTypeId, ct)`, and CreateResourceInstanceCommandDataProvider.GetResourceTypeAsync does `_dbContext.ResourceTypes.FirstOrDefaultAsync(t => t.Id == resourceTypeId, ct)` with NO IgnoreQueryFilters — so it goes through the global HasQueryFilter(x => x.DeletedAt == null), meaning a soft-deleted ResourceType (DeletedAt set) would return null from this query and be treated as 'Resource type not found.' by the handler. 5) Critical finding contradicting a soft-delete assumption: DELETE /resources/types/{id} is actually a HARD delete of the ResourceType row — DeleteResourceTypeCommandDataProvider.RemoveResourceType calls `_dbContext.ResourceTypes.Remove(resourceType)` (EF Remove, not a DeletedAt update), while its associated ResourceInstances are soft-deleted via SoftDeleteInstancesAsync's ExecuteUpdateAsync setting DeletedAt. Integration tests UpdateDeleteResourceTypeTests.cs explicitly assert the type row is gone 'even with IgnoreQueryFilters()' after delete (lines 185, 283), confirming hard delete despite ResourceType having a DeletedAt/IsDeleted property and a HasQueryFilter configured. 6) No integration test was found in ThingsBooksy.Modules.Resources.IntegrationTests that deletes a ResourceType and then asserts about the row's continued existence (soft-delete state) or re-creates a type with the same name after deletion; the closest related tests only cover duplicate-name-in-same-group (409), same-name-in-different-group (201/Created), and same-name-as-itself-on-update (success) — none re-create after delete. 7) One filtered/partial unique index pattern (HasIndex(...).HasFilter(...)) exists in the solution within the read paths available: ManagementGroupConfiguration.cs `builder.HasIndex(g => new { g.OwnerId, g.Name }).IsUnique().HasFilter("\"DeletedAt\" IS NULL")`, and ResourceInstanceConfiguration.cs uses a non-unique filtered index `HasIndex(i => new { i.GroupId, i.Id }).HasFilter("\"DeletedAt\" IS NULL")`. The ResourceType unique index (GroupId, Name) is the one index on these two entities that is NOT filtered.

notes: Answer covers all six sub-questions in Question 7. Note the surprising finding (5): DELETE /resources/types/{id} performs a hard delete of the ResourceType row (EF Remove) even though ResourceType has DeletedAt/IsDeleted and a query filter — only ResourceInstances are soft-deleted in the cascade. This means the uniqueness-index-vs-soft-delete question is somewhat moot for ResourceType itself since deleted rows are physically removed, not left behind with DeletedAt set; the unfiltered unique index on (GroupId, Name) therefore only constrains live rows in practice today, but would block re-use of a name by a soft-deleted (not yet hard-deleted) row if ResourceType.Delete() is ever called without RemoveResourceType (no such path was found in the read code). Item 5 (test that deletes then re-creates same name) — no such test found in Resources.IntegrationTests; only duplicate-name (409), cross-group same-name, and same-name-on-self-update scenarios exist.
